statement.text:
Let A be a finite group with a normal
                                      S a subgroup H. A subgroup U of H is
called an A-covering subgroup of H if    U = H. Is there a function f : N → N
                                          a∈A
such that whenever U < H < A, where A is a finite group, H is a normal subgroup
of A of index n, and U is an A-covering subgroup of H, the index |H : U | ⩽ f (n)?
(We have shown that the answer is “yes” if U is a maximal subgroup of H.)
   Comments of 2025: The conjecture is proved in the case where H acts innately
transitively on the coset space [H : U ] (M. Fusari, A. Previtali, P. Spiga, J. Group
Theory, 27 (2024), 929–965); for n = 3 with |H : U | ⩽ 10 (L. Gogniat, P. Spiga,
Preprint, 2025, https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.01287); and if H = U L where L is
a minimal A-invariant subgroup of H (M. Fusari, S. Harper, P. Spiga, Bull. Austral.
Math. Soc., 2025, https://doi.org/10.1017/S0004972725000176).
                                                           P. M. Neumann, C. E. Praeger
